newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tapie's film earnings targeted over bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Tapie's film earnings targeted over bankruptcy.

text.p: Bankrupt French businessman and former soccer boss Bernard Tapie suffered a new humiliation on Monday when liquidators said they wanted to seize his earnings made in a new career as a film star.

The court-appointed liquidators aim to seize three million francs ($585,000) they estimate Tapie will get for his role as a lawyer in the comedy "Men, Women: Instructions for Use" by director Claude Lelouch, which was released in France in August.
"We're just carrying out our mandate," said Yannick Pavec, one of two court-appointed liquidators seeking to track down Tapie's assets to cover his debts.
Pavec told Reuters a Paris commercial court would next month hear the call to seize Tapie's earnings from the film, which had been a bright spot for Tapie mired in debts.

Tapie is fighting a 1994 bankruptcy ruling, triggered by the state-owned Credit Lyonnais bank, which charges he owes it 1.2 billion francs ($235 million) after the collapse of a business empire that once ranged from running shoes to weighing machines.
Tapie is appealing against a ruling last week stripping him of his seat in the European Parliament. A former cabinet minister, he has also been forced to give up his French National Assembly seat.
The target of an avalanche of legal actions, Tapie is appealing against sentences of eight and six months in jail for tax fraud and rigging a soccer match.
